title: snapshot
description: Exact bytes obtained from one source at one time. A snapshot is the only object in this layer that may assert what is on a disk, and it asserts it about a NAMED location -- so a second machine that lacks the bytes disagrees with the `locations` list, not with the manifest.

from.description: the URI the bytes came from

via.description: the pipeline that fetched them, when it is not a direct download

relocated_at.description: When these bytes were last moved on this machine. Distinct from `at`, which is when they were obtained from the source and never changes -- conflating the two makes a relocation look like a re-acquisition.

layout.description: 'source_native' means the upstream directory structure was preserved verbatim. It almost always should be: BIDS, NWB, zarr, Iceberg and parquet collections each have a layout their own tools expect, and rewriting them into one house style breaks every reader upstream ships.

locations.description: Where these bytes can currently be found. A LIST, and not part of the identity: adding an S3 mirror must not change what the snapshot is.

root.description: path relative to the data root

inventory.description: What is in it, per stream. Counts are exact unless a field says otherwise -- a sampled count and a corpus count are different numbers and must never be quoted interchangeably.

files.description: Every file, with its digest. This is what 'a run bottoms out in exact byte snapshots' actually means.

files_sidecar.description: Relative name of a TSV holding the per-file digests, used instead of an inline list when the file count would make the manifest unreadable.

files_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the file rows, so the sidecar cannot drift from the manifest unnoticed.
